item.title: Reading, writing, low-flying jets: San Jose Toxic Tour Blog
item.description: Washington Elementary School is under the direct flight path of the San Jose International Airport. As many as 10 jets fly overhead per hour, producing constant noise, fumes and exhaust, that disrupt students’ education and possibly their health as well.

item.title: Noisy neighborhood? One family lives with it: SJ Toxic Tour Blog
item.description: By Donovan Farnham and Isaiah Guzman Alison Soman, her husband John and their five-year-old son Ben live in perhaps the loudest area in San Jose. Their home in the Newhall-Sherwood neighborhood sits within steps of Highway 880, a train yard sits about 1,500 feet to the east and San Jose International Airport is just beyond […]

item.title: In smoggy Los Angeles, one neighborhood pushes back
item.description: News about Boyle Heights in Los Angeles tends to be about crime or gentrification. There's little coverage of air pollution, lack of safe and green spaces, lack of access to affordable and healthy food options — or the residents and organizations that are determined to change this.

item.title: Young people define a healthy future for Boyle Heights
item.description: New community collaborations in Los Angeles are giving young people a leading role in improving their communities.

item.title: Washington Elementary students need microphones to talk
item.description: Students at Washington Elementary School have to take turns using wireless microphones to be heard over the continuous noise from airplanes from the nearby San Jose International Airport.

item.title: ‘Right Beneath Our Feet’: The Toxic Tour returns to Oakland
item.description: Thinking about planting a garden this spring? Many West Oakland residents are doing the same — unaware that there is lead and cadmium in the soil and perhaps an old gasoline tank right under their driveway.

item.title: Los Angeles neighborhood bears the brunt of air pollution
item.description: As summer temperatures rise, so do fears of asthma and other illnesses caused by all the air pollution converging on the east Los Angeles community of Boyle Heights.
